body.value: A narrative exhibit reads as prose beside a canvas — the story on one side, the object it's about on the other.
Click a section and the canvas switches to its object and fits the framed view; the active section lights up in the spine.
Scroll the spine and the canvas follows along.

none: Archie turns images into annotated exhibits — no server, no database, no lock-in. This library holds every exhibit you're building; open one to start.
An exhibit's overview is itself a canvas: drag objects to set their reading order, and the count badge shows how many notes each one carries.
Draw a region, write the note in the popover anchored right where you drew it — the marker follows as you pan and zoom.
The same object, read more than one way: a Reading is a mutually-exclusive interpretive pass, and the legend lets a visitor switch between them.
Sequence sections into a narrative spine — bind prose to an object and a framed region, and the reader's camera follows the story.
Drag across the waveform to mark a time range, or import a VTT/SRT transcript to seed a whole recording's worth of notes at once.
Video adds a spatial dimension: draw a box on a paused frame and set a time window — a combined spatiotemporal selector.
A Map is a fourth medium: regions anchor to true longitude/latitude, so re-framing the basemap keeps them nailed to the Earth.
Cmd+K opens the cite palette — reach any note or exhibit in the library and insert a live, clickable reference.
Set the exhibit's title, rights, and required statement here — the same fields that carry through to the published IIIF manifest.
Drop a folder, paste a IIIF manifest URL, or drag in files directly — the import gate that once required a IIIF server is open.
Publish bakes the whole library into static HTML, JSON, and media — a folder, a zip, or straight to GitHub Pages.
Every action in Studio has a keyboard shortcut — this sheet is always one keystroke away.
Visitors land on the gallery — every published exhibit in the library, one card each.
The reader pairs the deep-zoom canvas with a sidebar of notes; select one and its region solos on the canvas.
A narrative exhibit reads as prose beside a canvas — scroll the spine and the canvas follows, fitting the framed view for each section as you go.
Audio and video play inline with a transcript spine — each line seeks the recording as you read down the page.
The finder searches every note, object, and exhibit in the library at once — press the shortcut and start typing.
A note with an image of its own opens into a full-screen lightbox — the note text stays alongside it.
Long notes expand into a centred reading sheet over a dimmed backdrop — room to actually read, with the Readings legend and citations still in reach.
Drop <archie-viewer> into any page — a read-only Web Component, about half the Studio's bundle, no build step, no unsafe-eval.
